name: Strasserism
summary: Strasserism is the 'German socialism' of Otto Strasser and, in the 1925/26 programme, of his brother Gregor: a dissident current of National Socialism that broke with Hitler in 1930. It makes the nation the sole owner of land, raw materials and the means of production, which individuals and 'factory fellowships' of manager, workers and State hold in hereditary fief, and replaces parties and parliament with vocational councils and Chambers of Estates under a president elected for life, in a federal Germany of provinces. It rejects Marxism, class struggle, capitalism and the totalitarian State alike; its early programme excluded Jews from citizenship, while Strasser's later writings proposed minority rights and a European federation.
scope: Otto Strasser's doctrine as the defining sources tie it to him: the 1925/26 Strasser programme (Kühnl, s8, s9), the Aufbau des deutschen Sozialismus of 1931 and 1936 with the Black Front's manifestos, reprinted with Strasser's 1940 peace proposals in Germany Tomorrow (s7), as treated by Gottfried (s10) and Hughes (s11). The Aufbau, held and republished from 1931 to 1940, is taken as the mature position; where the 1925/26 draft (withdrawn in 1926) or the 1940 proposals differ, the answer records the change. Hitler and I (s1) is used sparingly, as historians doubt its self-portrait. Gregor Strasser's separate 1932 positions and the neo-Strasserism of later groups are other subjects and are excluded.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: The Aufbau calls the abandonment of the international gold standard an essential preliminary to autarchy and attacks gold's legal privilege over all other commodities.

no-central-bank.rationale: The Aufbau keeps a State Reichsbank that issues banknotes and sets the official rate of interest.

return-to-pre-conversion-religion.rationale: The Aufbau calls any attempt to eliminate Christianity from the West foolish and impracticable, and Hitler and I records Strasser's objection to Rosenberg's paganism.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Strasser's 1940 programme disavows any valuation of peoples as better or worse, since all have equal rights, needs and duties by the will of the Creator.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: The Aufbau has German education concentrate on producing a knightly, chivalrous ideal type as the nation's elite.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: Gregor Strasser's text in Germany Tomorrow holds that work is more than possession and achievement more than dividends, and the Aufbau ends the rule of capital over workers.

maximum-personal-income.rationale: The Aufbau fixes maximum and minimum incomes only during the transition and afterwards sets no limit to acquisition beyond a man's working powers.

avoid-permanent-military-alliances.rationale: Germany Tomorrow commits members of the European Federation to combine against any attack on one of them.

regional-resource-ownership.rationale: The Aufbau vests land and raw materials in the whole nation, not in the provinces where they lie.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: Strasser's Kampfgemeinschaft revolutionärer Nationalsozialisten called itself a school of officers and non-commissioned officers of the German revolution.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The 1925/26 programme expelled Jews who had arrived since 1914, but Strasser's 1940 programme keeps minorities in Germany with equal rights.

physical-labour-duty.rationale: The Aufbau requires a year of labour service in which every young German of both sexes learns a handicraft.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: The Aufbau condemns parties for sundering the people into factions and fostering oppositions, and makes their destruction the condition of a commonwealth.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: The Aufbau encourages voluntary producers' cooperatives but rules out any material favouring of them by the State.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: The Aufbau rejects the creed that man is sent into the world in order to work and treats labour as only a means of life.

refuse-to-join-illegitimate-government.rationale: The Aufbau's postface says the movement must ruthlessly oppose any participation in a coalition with the old system.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: The 1925/26 programme gave the vote in the vocational chambers at 21.

students-direct-own-learning.rationale: The Aufbau decides admission to university by the will of the community through teachers and examiners, not by what pupils want.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: The Aufbau abolishes the existing scale and method of taxation in favour of tithes, imposts and guild lump sums, leaving the inheritance tax and a few luxury taxes as the only old taxes.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: The Aufbau holds that whoever uses liberal weapons to defeat a liberal system will fail, and opposes any democratic choice.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: The Aufbau asks revolutionaries to stake their lives, and the Black Front called Germans to arms against Hitler.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: Germany Tomorrow calls for cultural collaboration in the European Federation, an 'Olympiad of the mind', a European Academy and high schools teaching in foreign tongues.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: The 1936 postface tells German socialists to work for the overthrow of the Hitler system with any and every means, and the Black Front called for armed revolt.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The Aufbau says the land available for the community is owned exclusively by the nation, whose organizational form is the State, and is only leased out in entail.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Germany Tomorrow holds that joint economic advantages, including the abolition of customs barriers, are the strongest cement of the European Federation.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: Germany Tomorrow requires every member of the European Federation to recognise its arbitral powers and the Permanent Court of International Justice.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Workers in the factory fellowship receive wages suited to their achievements besides a small profit share, so wage labour remains.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: Germany Tomorrow says Germany must atone for its complicity in Hitler's violence, repudiate it on principle and pay reparations to Poland and Czechoslovakia.

conquest-no-lawful-claim.rationale: Germany Tomorrow demands the cancellation of the results of Hitler's conquest and holds that right, not might, must prevail between nations.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The Aufbau demands a comprehensive national insurance covering childhood, unemployment, accident, old age and death, so that no member of the community goes hungry. notes: Later pass (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-09) bringing the 2026-10-15 audit to rules 5, prompted by search traffic (closest ideology of Nick Fuentes). The first pass rested mostly on Wikipedia (s2, s3, s5, s6), on Hitler and I (s1) and on an Ossietzky review (s4) that could not be reopened; every answer was checked against Strasser's own programmes, now read in full: Germany Tomorrow (s7, containing the Aufbau and the Black Front manifestos) and the 1925/26 programme printed by Kühnl (s9), with Kühnl (s8), Gottfried (s10) and Hughes (s11) as scholarship. Answers resting only on the old sources were changed or nulled, the old version kept in reviewHistory. Strasserism never governed, so it has no record: every source is words. Strasser's positions changed: the 1925/26 draft demanded the 1914 borders, colonies, a 'national dictatorship', protective tariffs and the reclassification of Jews as foreigners without the vote, while the Aufbau (1931/1936) and the 1940 proposals reject the totalitarian State and imperialism, separate Church and State, open Europe to free trade and settlement and promise equal rights and minority status. Where the texts take opposite sides the answer is 0 at low confidence. Hughes (s11) argues that Strasser remained an antisemite and whitewashed his past, which the answers do not override since they follow the programmes' stated positions. Themes searched: economy (property, entail, factory fellowships, planning, money, taxes, insurance), government (estates, president, provinces, parties, officials), liberty (press, religion, punishment), means (revolution, violence, elections), society (race, minorities, Jews, schools, family), world (Versailles, Europe, colonies, disarmament, Bolshevism), technology and ecology (de-urbanization, machines). Not available: the 1929 Fourteen Theses of the German Revolution (only in the Lane and Rupp anthology, which was not found in a publisher's or library's open copy) and Strasser's post-war Der Faschismus and solidarism writings; Ossietzky's review (s4) was read in its original 1932 Weltbühne printing: it quotes the 1931 first edition of the Aufbau as stripping citizenship from a German who marries a member of another people and as denying Jews citizenship and fiefs, passages absent from the 1940 English text; since the 1931 edition could not be checked, these quotations are not used as evidence, but they show that the 1940 text's minority rights are a later change.
